summary: The SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes, revises, and expands federal programs and funding related to substance use disorders, overdoses, mental health, child trauma, and fetal alcohol spectrum disorders through fiscal year 2030.

affected_groups.effect: Receive reauthorized and expanded federal grants and technical assistance for substance use prevention, overdose reversal drug distribution, and regional support services.
affected_groups.group: State, Tribal, and local government entities and first responders

affected_groups.effect: Gain access to targeted outreach, residential treatment programs, fetal alcohol spectrum disorder support services, and expanded youth trauma and prevention initiatives.
affected_groups.group: Pregnant and postpartum women and children

affected_groups.effect: Eligible for educational loan repayments, training grant programs, and expanded prescriber education organizations under updated federal rules.
affected_groups.group: Health care practitioners and behavioral health workforce

affected_groups.effect: Benefit from expanded recovery housing, peer-run training and technical assistance centers, and workforce support programs that include transportation services.

key_provisions: Reauthorizes and expands Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) programs addressing drug prevention, overdose monitoring, and first responder overdose reversal drug training.
Reestablishes and expands Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) activities regarding fetal alcohol spectrum disorders, including research, awareness, and support services.
Requires the 9-8-8 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline network administrator and participating local and regional crisis centers to report cybersecurity vulnerabilities and incidents.
Reauthorizes and revises the Residential Treatment for Pregnant and Postpartum Women program, allowing targeted outreach to women disproportionately impacted by maternal substance use disorders.

Reauthorizes health workforce education, training, and loan repayment programs through Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) to support practitioners in substance use disorder treatment and mental health.
Expands the CAREER Act and related workforce development programs to support individuals in treatment and recovery, authorizing funds for transportation services and employment outcome reporting.

Amends the Controlled Substances Act to allow pharmacies to deliver certain self-administered schedule III-V controlled substances to prescribing practitioners under risk evaluation and mitigation strategies.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The SUPPORT for Patients and Communities Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes, revises, and expands federal programs and funding related to substance use disorders, overdoses, mental health, child trauma, and fetal alcohol spectrum disorders through fiscal year 2030.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates and extends numerous federal health, education, and labor programs focused on the opioid crisis, mental health services, and addiction treatment through fiscal year 2030, impacting federal funding allocations, agency oversight, and grant structures nationwide.
